recommended_title: Width and Delayed Generalization in Finite-Horizon Modular Addition
central_question: How does hidden width relate to the separation between training-set fitting and held-out generalization in a fixed modular-addition network under finite training horizons and matched regularization controls?
central_thesis: The retained comparisons show earlier fitting at larger widths without monotone short-horizon generalization, while two longer-horizon width-128 delayed events remain conditional observations rather than qualified evidence of a size law or a decay-clock mechanism.
narrative_rationale: A conditional empirical study is supported by paired width, seed, and arm records, unlike a mechanistic explanation or a search-success story. The studied configuration has no sustained generalization onset in the short-horizon records, but two retained width-128 final records do have delayed onsets. Three final width-32 records remain censored and all final width-256 records are absent. Final evaluation completed but did not qualify. These facts support a coherent account of what this experiment establishes and leaves unidentified, not a universal claim about width, a causal horizon comparison, or superiority. Readiness means a supportable writing plan, not scientific qualification or a prediction of venue acceptance.

The status value denotes rejection of an inherited untested mechanism story, not rejection of an existing paper. staged_input_impact: No previous_paper, aggregated, extra_tasks, or edit-context inputs are present; there is no manuscript to preserve, broaden, or recenter.
Direct inspection of the local selected controller and evaluator establishes one fixed embedding-sum GELU architecture with common hyperparameters, not a new architecture or adaptive training method.

The final_evaluation block is independently decisive: completed but not_qualified, with five retained width-seed records and four missing records. It changes the framing from an optimization-success narrative to a conditional, incomplete-evidence study.

method_groups.name: Common-configuration width sweep
method_groups.include_reason: The studied condition uses learning rate 0.003, AdamW weight decay 1.0, and initialization multiplier 0.5 across widths 32, 128, and 256. Call it the studied configuration, not a novel optimizer or a proven winner. Final evidence exists only for widths 32 and 128.

method_groups.name: Fixed reference
method_groups.include_reason: Retain the original measured comparison: learning rate 0.001, weight decay 1.0, initialization multiplier 1.0, same width/seed/split/horizon. It differs in both learning rate and initialization, so it is a reference rather than an isolated-component test. Compare only paired retained records and do not assert global validity after failed final qualification.

method_groups.name: Zero-weight-decay control
method_groups.include_reason: Matches the studied learning rate, initialization, width, and split while setting decay to zero. Separates observed finite-horizon behavior with and without decay; it cannot establish that decay is universally necessary or that the delay is a decay clock.

method_groups.name: Matched-initial-global-norm control
method_groups.include_reason: Globally rescales the initial parameters to the same-seed width-128 norm. Tests a limited initial-norm alternative, not complete capacity or functional matching. At width 128 this arm duplicates the studied condition, including retained hashes and scientific metric trajectories, so it is not an independent replication or an extra event.

results_focus: Lead with a complete final availability table: widths 32/128/256 by seeds 60613/70717/80821; observed records are 3/2/0 respectively. Explicitly disclose failed final qualification in the main text, not just the supplement.

Compare raw held-out endpoint accuracies across widths and the four arms within each evaluation setting. The studied short-horizon width-32 records have higher endpoint accuracy than widths 128 and 256 despite later fitting; do not turn this into a universal inverse-size law.

Compare fitting and sustained held-out onset directly, with censor arrows: short-horizon records at 6000 updates versus separately labeled final records at 24000. Final width-128 fitting/onset pairs are 300/17600 and 200/19200 updates; final width-32 fitting occurs at 2600, 2400, and 3000 with no observed held-out onset by 24000.

Use the fixed reference, zero-decay, and norm-matched arms as within-record controls. Retained final reference and zero-decay arms have no sustained held-out onset; the width-128 norm arm duplicates the studied event, not an additional result.

Treat the two horizons as separate evidence blocks under one question: data pools and seed sets also change. No same-seed, same-pool horizon intervention or causal claim that longer training reverses a width ranking is available.

The intended final width-256-minus-width-32 contrast and corresponding interactions are unidentified because width-256 records are absent; final paired_contrasts are null. Missing records are not zero accuracy observations, right-censored trajectories, or measured losses.

Show every seed value and paired differences where supported. Do not use checkpoints or examples as independent trials. Small-seed descriptive variation is the main uncertainty display; any additional uncertainty calculation must be derived reproducibly from retained data and labeled conditional on availability.
